description: NULL handling in aggregate functions: empty table behaviour, COUNT(NULL), SUM(NULL)

steps.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM empty_t
steps.note: COUNT(*) on empty table returns 0, not NULL

steps.sql: SELECT COUNT(val) AS cnt FROM empty_t
steps.note: COUNT(col) on empty table returns 0, not NULL

steps.sql: SELECT SUM(val) AS s FROM empty_t
steps.note: SUM on empty table returns NULL (SQLite rule)

steps.sql: SELECT AVG(val) AS a FROM empty_t
steps.note: AVG on empty table returns NULL (SQLite rule)

steps.sql: SELECT MIN(val) AS mn FROM empty_t
steps.note: MIN on empty table returns NULL (SQLite rule)

steps.sql: SELECT MAX(val) AS mx FROM empty_t
steps.note: MAX on empty table returns NULL (SQLite rule)

steps.sql: SELECT COUNT(x) AS cnt FROM nulls_t
steps.note: COUNT(col) skips NULLs — only 2 non-NULL values

steps.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM nulls_t
steps.note: COUNT(*) counts all rows including NULLs

steps.sql: SELECT SUM(x) AS s FROM nulls_t
